title: How we separated AI dialogue from world logic in a browser RPG
author: Complete-Ranger1512
selftext:
We’re JENGA, the team behind You & Me: Level Up, a dark-fantasy RPG that runs in a browser. One part of the project might be useful to other devs here: giving AI adventurers something to say without giving the model control of the game.

A simulation handles movement, which zone a character visits, and leveling. Claude or a local Qwen model handles occasional dialogue, with the game passing in a small amount of context about the place and the character. We keep chat generation out of the gameplay loop. That way a slow answer or a skipped model call doesn’t stop an adventurer from walking around town. For the same reason, the model isn’t a source of truth for items or player progression.

If you’re building something similar, the separation is the part I’d start with. The NPC remains useful as a game character even when all of its lines are scripted or it has nothing to say. It also makes the conversation system easier to evaluate in isolation. We used AI-assisted tooling elsewhere in development and for some assets and translations as well.

The game is in free open beta with optional in-game purchases. If you’re curious about the project, it’s here: [https://nrnrlv.com/?lang=en](https://nrnrlv.com/?lang=en)
